D018-D020_h001.question:
I’ve been having these awful dreams about the robbery at the gas station where I work—same thing every few nights: the guy pointing the gun, me dropping the register money. It makes me wake up sweating, heart slamming, and I don’t calm down for ages. I keep reliving it, feel ashamed, like I should’ve done something different, even though deep down I know I couldn’t have. I blame the manager—he wasn’t even there that night, left me alone during the late shift. I used to be focused, but now I can’t even decide what to eat or what shirt to wear without getting stuck. I don’t care about much anymore—stopped going out, lost interest in applying for mechanic school like I used to want.  

It’s been about four months since it happened. I know it wasn’t my fault, but I still feel broken. The dreams and jumpiness haven’t gone away, but honestly, it’s not like I’m scared *all* the time or constantly reliving it in flashbacks. I just can’t bounce back like I thought I would. I wanted help before it gets worse, especially since I’m still working nights.

D018-D020_h002.question:
I’ve been really struggling since my best friend passed away in that car accident three months ago. It hit me hard—she was like a sister to me. Lately, I keep having these nightmares about the crash, and I wake up shaking, like I can feel it happening all over again. I don’t sleep well at all. My husband says I flinch whenever the door slams or the phone dings suddenly—it scares me how jumpy I’ve become. 

I’ve pulled back from a lot of people. I used to meet up with friends weekly for coffee, but now I cancel plans. It feels easier to just stay home. I even missed a team meeting at work because I couldn’t decide what to wear—sounds silly, but I stood in front of my closet for twenty minutes, frozen. I keep wondering if I could’ve done something—if I’d called her that night, maybe she wouldn’t have been driving. I know logically it doesn’t make sense, but I can’t shake it.

It’s been several months now, and while some things are a bit better, I’m still not back to myself. The dreams and fear haven’t gone away completely, but honestly, I don’t think I’ve had enough of the symptoms long enough—or intensely enough—to meet some formal trauma diagnosis. It’s just that everything since the accident feels… heavier.
D018-D020_h002.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D020_h003.question:
I’ve been struggling ever since the lab flooding three months ago—water damage, lost samples, months of work gone overnight. At first, I kept replaying it: the sound of rushing water, seeing my station submerged. Even now, if someone walks up behind me too quickly, I flinch hard, heart racing—it’s like my body can’t forget. I see lab coats out of the corner of my eye and I tense up. 

But the worst part is… I just don’t feel anything. I used to love analyzing data—there was joy in the patterns. Now it’s just… static. I can’t connect with my husband like before. I try, but it’s like I’m numb. I keep thinking, *If I’d just backed up the raw sequences off-site, maybe it wouldn’t have been so bad.* Some days the guilt is crushing. And honestly? I’ve been blaming the facilities team—they knew the pipes were old. I know that’s not fair, but I can’t shake it.

Making decisions feels impossible. What to wear, what to eat—everything stalls me. It’s been over a month now, and while it’s not getting worse, it’s not better either. I function, but just barely. I don’t think this qualifies as PTSD—they said that usually involves constant nightmares or reliving it, which I don’t really have. But something’s off.
D018-D020_h003.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D020_h004.question:

It started about a month after the crash, and it still hasn’t let up. But no, I wouldn’t say I’m haunted every day, or that I avoid *everything* related to cars—I drive when I need to. It’s just… everything feels heavier now, and I can’t seem to steady myself. It’s not that I have flashbacks like in war films. It’s just this constant, raw reaction—to little things, to nothing at all.

    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D020_h006.question:

Some parts, though, I just can’t remember—like how I got the tractor out. I know I did, but the details? Gone. I try not to think about it. I’ve stopped going near that part of the property. 

I don’t feel like myself. Most days I feel hollow, like I’m just going through motions. My wife says I don’t laugh anymore. I snap at her over small things—dropped a tray last week and I yelled like she’d ruined everything. And if one of the kids touches me from behind, I jump out of my skin. 

It started right after the fire, and it’s been over a month now. I know it wasn’t combat or a war zone, and I don’t have all those symptoms the counselor mentioned when I went in—like constant nightmares or being on guard all the time. Truth is, I’m just not coping like I used to. I expected to bounce back, but I haven’t.

    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D020_h007.question:

Those images just pop up—outta nowhere—when I’m editing scripts or even brushing my teeth. I avoid the subway station near my old place and won’t go near anything with smoke alarms now. But here’s the thing—these reactions, the fear, the gaps… they’re bad, but they don’t *fully* line up with what I’ve read about PTSD.     D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D020_h008.question:

I don’t have constant nightmares or persistent hyperarousal beyond what’s expected. My therapist said my reaction is severe, but it’s rooted in the stressor itself, not a full trauma syndrome. I’ve been feeling completely overwhelmed since my husband had that serious car accident three months ago. For weeks after, just hearing a siren or seeing an ambulance would send me into a spiral—I’d start shaking, my chest would tighten, and I couldn’t breathe. Even now, when our kids slam the car door too hard, I jump and feel like I’m back at the hospital waiting room. I’m constantly on edge, like something else is going to go wrong. I can’t relax, even at work where I used to feel so in control.  

The worst part is, I don’t feel *happy* anymore. My daughter got into her dream school last week—something we’ve been hoping for—and I just couldn’t summon any joy. I smiled for her sake, but inside, I was numb. That’s not me. I used to light up over little victories, both mine and my patients’. Now I just feel flat.  

And my temper… I snapped at a nurse for misplacing a chart—something I’d normally brush off. I feel guilty afterward, but it’s like the anger just bursts out.  

I know the accident was traumatic, but I don’t have flashbacks or nightmares about it—most of the time, I’m just stuck in this anxious fog. It’s been more than a month, and I’m still not back to myself, but I don’t feel like I “meet the criteria” for PTSD either. I just can’t seem to adjust.

I’ve been having a really hard time since that shooting call last month—first time I’ve ever been involved in something like that. Ever since, I can’t stop thinking about the sound of the gunfire, the way the victim looked… even just hearing a car backfire or a loud noise makes my chest tighten and I get flashbacks. I know it was bad, but I keep replaying it, and I just can’t seem to shake it.  

I’ve been angry all the time—little things set me off. Last week I yelled at a kid for jaywalking, like, way too hard. I even scared myself. My sergeant pulled me aside and said I don’t seem like myself. And honestly, I don’t feel like it. Even when I made it onto the honor roll last quarter—which used to mean everything—I felt… nothing. No pride, no joy, just empty.  

It’s been about ten weeks since the incident. I thought I’d bounce back by now, but instead I’m more on edge, sleeping weird, snapping at people. I don’t think I have PTSD—like, I’m not totally debilitated or avoiding everything, but this isn’t normal for me. It’s affecting my job, my focus. I know the trauma’s still with me, but I don’t meet all those criteria people talk about—just enough to ruin my days.
